concept.name: Nonfarm payrolls
concept.definition: The monthly change in the number of workers on U.S. nonfarm business and government payrolls, estimated by the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Current Employment Statistics (CES) survey of establishments. Released with the unemployment rate in The Employment Situation, it is the first major hard-data read on the U.S. economy each month.
concept.intuition: It answers 'how many jobs did employers actually add last month' from the business side, making it the market's favorite single labor-market number.
concept.mechanics: CES surveys about 119,000 businesses and government agencies covering roughly 622,000 worksites, using payroll records for the pay period including the 12th of the month. Estimates are seasonally adjusted, revised in each of the next two releases, and benchmarked annually to near-universe counts from unemployment-insurance tax records, with a birth-death model capturing new firms.
concept.formula: Net payroll change = Total nonfarm employment(t) - Total nonfarm employment(t-1), in thousands of jobs.
concept.failure_modes: First prints are revised twice and re-benchmarked annually (the 2025 benchmark cut about 862,000 jobs from 2025 estimates), and strikes or severe weather can distort a single month by hundreds of thousands.
concept.misconceptions: It counts jobs, not people - a worker with two payroll jobs appears twice - and it excludes farm workers, the self-employed, and unpaid family workers, so it can diverge from the household-survey employment count.
concept.example: In April 2020 nonfarm payrolls fell by roughly 20.5 million, the largest one-month drop on record; the June 2020 rebound of about 4.8 million was the largest gain.
